s1.syndrome_frame: Acute monocular vision loss with associated orbital and adnexal inflammation
salient_findings: Pain, numbness, and erythematous induration of the eyelids and forearm
Tense eyelid edema, chemosis, and corneal haze
Serous retinal detachment and macular whitening
key_facts: Patient is an obese man in his mid-30s
No prior systemic or ocular disorders
Heavy alcohol consumption and buprenorphine/naloxone use the night prior
Denies any trauma
Visual acuity is no light perception in the right eye and 20/20 in the left eye
Intraocular pressure is 37 mm Hg in the right eye and 21 mm Hg in the left eye
Creatinine level is 2.2 mg/dL
Creatine kinase level is 29,320 U/L
Periorbital soft-tissue swelling on noncontrast computed tomography
Severe disorganization of the retinal architecture on Optical Coherence Tomography
Delayed choroidal filling and poor vascular perfusion on Fluorescein Angiography

shortlist.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden vision loss, no light perception in one eye, and retinal findings on imaging

shortlist.label: Posterior Scleritis
shortlist.why_kept: Orbital and adnexal inflammation, elevated intraocular pressure, and retinal detachment

shortlist.label: Giant Cell Arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute monocular vision loss, orbital inflammation, and elevated creatinine and creatine kinase levels

shortlist.label: Cavernous Sinus Thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Severe vision loss, orbital swelling, and elevated intraocular pressure

shortlist.label: Tolosa-Hunt Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Acute monocular vision loss, orbital and adnexal inflammation, and cranial nerve involvement

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with vision loss, periorbital edema, chemosis, and elevated intraocular pressure in one eye, combined with laboratory findings of elevated creatinine and creatine kinase levels, suggests a systemic condition. The absence of prior ocular disorders and the presence of heavy alcohol consumption and buprenorphine/naloxone use the night prior may have contributed to a hypercoagulable state, increasing the risk for cavernous sinus thrombosis. The imaging studies, including periorbital soft-tissue swelling on CT and severe disorganization of the retinal architecture on OCT, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
rejected.why: While this condition could explain the vision loss and retinal findings, it does not account for the periorbital edema, chemosis, and systemic laboratory abnormalities.

rejected.label: Posterior Scleritis
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with pain, redness, and decreased vision, but the patient's laboratory and imaging findings suggest a more systemic condition.

rejected.label: Giant Cell Arteritis
rejected.why: This condition is more common in older adults and typically presents with headache, jaw claudication, and visual symptoms, which are not prominent in this case.

rejected.label: Tolosa-Hunt Syndrome
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with painful ophthalmoplegia and may have some similar imaging findings, but the patient's laboratory and systemic findings are not consistent with this diagnosis.
